character: Warden Isolde, keeper of the Waystone Camp
text_with_cues: [softly] There you are. I felt the waystone hum the moment you woke.
subtitle: There you are. I felt the waystone hum the moment you woke.

character: Warden Isolde, keeper of the Waystone Camp
text_with_cues: Easy, now. Everyone wakes a little lost. The Afterworld is like that. It listens before it speaks.
subtitle: Easy, now. Everyone wakes a little lost. The Afterworld is like that. It listens before it speaks.

character: Warden Isolde, keeper of the Waystone Camp
text_with_cues: I'm Isolde, Warden of this camp. We keep the waystones lit, and we keep travellers like you on your feet.
subtitle: I'm Isolde, Warden of this camp. We keep the waystones lit, and we keep travellers like you on your feet.

character: Warden Isolde, keeper of the Waystone Camp
text_with_cues: A world still deciding what it wants to be. Old rules, half forgotten, written into stone and storm.
subtitle: A world still deciding what it wants to be. Old rules, half forgotten, written into stone and storm.

character: Warden Isolde, keeper of the Waystone Camp
text_with_cues: We call those rules Edicts. A few folk carry one inside them, the way you do. That's why the world noticed you.
subtitle: We call those rules Edicts. A few folk carry one inside them, the way you do. That's why the world noticed you.

character: Warden Isolde, keeper of the Waystone Camp
text_with_cues: Walk far enough and you'll see. Stones that forget to fall. A bell that rings and takes the memory with it. A king who keeps time in a vault.
subtitle: Walk far enough and you'll see. Stones that forget to fall. A bell that rings and takes the memory with it. A king who keeps time in a vault.

character: Warden Isolde, keeper of the Waystone Camp
text_with_cues: None of it's cruel, exactly. But it remembers what you do. Every kindness, and every grudge.
subtitle: None of it's cruel, exactly. But it remembers what you do. Every kindness, and every grudge.

character: Warden Isolde, keeper of the Waystone Camp
text_with_cues: First things first. Lay your hand on the waystone, there on the dais. Once it knows you, it will always bring you home.
subtitle: First things first. Lay your hand on the waystone, there on the dais. Once it knows you, it will always bring you home.

character: Warden Isolde, keeper of the Waystone Camp
text_with_cues: Then let out the Edict that lives in you, and go and see Marta at the forge. She'll teach you how not to die. [dryly] Mostly.
subtitle: Then let out the Edict that lives in you, and go and see Marta at the forge. She'll teach you how not to die. Mostly.

character: Warden Isolde, keeper of the Waystone Camp
text_with_cues: The waystone first. Touch it, and it'll learn your name.
subtitle: The waystone first. Touch it, and it'll learn your name.

character: Warden Isolde, keeper of the Waystone Camp
text_with_cues: Go on, let the Edict out. Whatever it does, it's yours. The camp has seen worse.
subtitle: Go on, let the Edict out. Whatever it does, it's yours. The camp has seen worse.

character: Warden Isolde, keeper of the Waystone Camp
text_with_cues: Marta's at the forge, west of the dais. Follow the sound of hammering. [amused] And the swearing.
subtitle: Marta's at the forge, west of the dais. Follow the sound of hammering. And the swearing.

character: Warden Isolde, keeper of the Waystone Camp
text_with_cues: Marta will have you rolling in the dirt by now. Good. Dodge first, parry second, and pride last of all.
subtitle: Marta will have you rolling in the dirt by now. Good. Dodge first, parry second, and pride last of all.

character: Warden Isolde, keeper of the Waystone Camp
text_with_cues: Open your journal. It writes down everything the world tells you, so you don't have to.
subtitle: Open your journal. It writes down everything the world tells you, so you don't have to.

character: Warden Isolde, keeper of the Waystone Camp
text_with_cues: Bram's at the supply stall, east of the dais. He'll teach you what a Mark is worth. To the copper.
subtitle: Bram's at the supply stall, east of the dais. He'll teach you what a Mark is worth. To the copper.

character: Warden Isolde, keeper of the Waystone Camp
text_with_cues: You're ready, then. Good. The camp can only hold you so long, and the world won't wait.
subtitle: You're ready, then. Good. The camp can only hold you so long, and the world won't wait.

character: Warden Isolde, keeper of the Waystone Camp
text_with_cues: Take work from the Warden's Board, there by the dais. Coin, reputation, and a reason to see the wilds.
subtitle: Take work from the Warden's Board, there by the dais. Coin, reputation, and a reason to see the wilds.

character: Warden Isolde, keeper of the Waystone Camp
text_with_cues: Then follow the tremors. Where the ground hums, an Edict has slipped loose. Bind it before it binds something else.
subtitle: Then follow the tremors. Where the ground hums, an Edict has slipped loose. Bind it before it binds something else.

character: Warden Isolde, keeper of the Waystone Camp
text_with_cues: Find a shrine on the Pilgrim's road, and touch the waystone at one of the old landmarks. Then come back and tell me everything.
subtitle: Find a shrine on the Pilgrim's road, and touch the waystone at one of the old landmarks. Then come back and tell me everything.

character: Warden Isolde, keeper of the Waystone Camp
text_with_cues: The waystones answer the ones they know. While you're on the road, a pillar of light stands over the place you're bound for.
subtitle: The waystones answer the ones they know. While you're on the road, a pillar of light stands over the place you're bound for.

character: Warden Isolde, keeper of the Waystone Camp
text_with_cues: Press G to change which place it marks, if you're chasing more than one thing at once.
subtitle: Press G to change which place it marks, if you're chasing more than one thing at once.

character: Warden Isolde, keeper of the Waystone Camp
text_with_cues: The Board, the tremor, the shrine, the landmark. One at a time, or all at once. Your mark will show you.
subtitle: The Board, the tremor, the shrine, the landmark. One at a time, or all at once. Your mark will show you.

character: Warden Isolde, keeper of the Waystone Camp
text_with_cues: So it's true. An Edict came to your hand, and the shrine didn't turn you away.
subtitle: So it's true. An Edict came to your hand, and the shrine didn't turn you away.

character: Warden Isolde, keeper of the Waystone Camp
text_with_cues: Then I'll tell you what the Wardens don't tell everyone. Three old powers wait out there. The Bell-Ringer in the Hollow Cathedral. The King of Seconds, deep in his vault. And the Pilgrim, who walks and never arrives.
subtitle: Then I'll tell you what the Wardens don't tell everyone. Three old powers wait out there. The Bell-Ringer in the Hollow Cathedral. The King of Seconds, deep in his vault. And the Pilgrim, who walks and never arrives.

character: Warden Isolde, keeper of the Waystone Camp
text_with_cues: They're why the world is stuck. Free them, or face them. Either way, it starts to move again. [quietly] And whatever they leave behind is yours to carry.
subtitle: They're why the world is stuck. Free them, or face them. Either way, it starts to move again. And whatever they leave behind is yours to carry.

character: Warden Isolde, keeper of the Waystone Camp
text_with_cues: The cathedral lies south and west, under a bell nobody remembers hearing. The vault goes down a long way, past the old roads.
subtitle: The cathedral lies south and west, under a bell nobody remembers hearing. The vault goes down a long way, past the old roads.

character: Warden Isolde, keeper of the Waystone Camp
text_with_cues: The Pilgrim you'll hear before you see. Its footsteps wear roads into the grass. Wren can mark any of them for you.
subtitle: The Pilgrim you'll hear before you see. Its footsteps wear roads into the grass. Wren can mark any of them for you.

character: Warden Isolde, keeper of the Waystone Camp
text_with_cues: The Bell-Ringer, the King and the Pilgrim. Rest when you need to. The camp will always be here.
subtitle: The Bell-Ringer, the King and the Pilgrim. Rest when you need to. The camp will always be here.

character: Warden Isolde, keeper of the Waystone Camp
text_with_cues: [quietly] Listen. The bell is quiet. The clocks have stopped arguing. And somewhere, a stone pilgrim is finally sitting down.
subtitle: Listen. The bell is quiet. The clocks have stopped arguing. And somewhere, a stone pilgrim is finally sitting down.

character: Warden Isolde, keeper of the Waystone Camp
text_with_cues: But the world has five more locks on it. Five Wardens, set to guard the lands when the old powers fell asleep. They never stopped guarding.
subtitle: But the world has five more locks on it. Five Wardens, set to guard the lands when the old powers fell asleep. They never stopped guarding.

character: Warden Isolde, keeper of the Waystone Camp
text_with_cues: A samurai of ash in the blossom country. A lich who will not stay dead. A colossus in the white waste. A sentinel under the sun. And a gilded warden who judges everyone who passes.
subtitle: A samurai of ash in the blossom country. A lich who will not stay dead. A colossus in the white waste. A sentinel under the sun. And a gilded warden who judges everyone who passes.

character: Warden Isolde, keeper of the Waystone Camp
text_with_cues: Each one has a trial before it will even face you. The keepers know the ways in. Ask them.
subtitle: Each one has a trial before it will even face you. The keepers know the ways in. Ask them.

character: Warden Isolde, keeper of the Waystone Camp
text_with_cues: Go to the Lantern Dojo in Petalfall. His last disciple still keeps it. Win the Duel of Lanterns and you'll earn the right to challenge him.
subtitle: Go to the Lantern Dojo in Petalfall. His last disciple still keeps it. Win the Duel of Lanterns and you'll earn the right to challenge him.

character: Warden Isolde, keeper of the Waystone Camp
text_with_cues: Sister Ines has been reading the crypt records. Three crypts, three phylacteries. Break them all, or he'll simply get up again.
subtitle: Sister Ines has been reading the crypt records. Three crypts, three phylacteries. Break them all, or he'll simply get up again.

character: Warden Isolde, keeper of the Waystone Camp
text_with_cues: Torvald has seen its tracks. If you've hunted with him, you know how to follow them. Don't lose the trail in the snow.
subtitle: Torvald has seen its tracks. If you've hunted with him, you know how to follow them. Don't lose the trail in the snow.

character: Warden Isolde, keeper of the Waystone Camp
text_with_cues: Rashid's people tell of a temple under the dunes that only opens to the sun. You'll need to bend the light.
subtitle: Rashid's people tell of a temple under the dunes that only opens to the sun. You'll need to bend the light.

character: Warden Isolde, keeper of the Waystone Camp
text_with_cues: The Gilded Vault won't open without five glyph tablets. They're scattered through the old places. Wren has a list. [amused] Of course she does.
subtitle: The Gilded Vault won't open without five glyph tablets. They're scattered through the old places. Wren has a list. Of course she does.

character: Warden Isolde, keeper of the Waystone Camp
text_with_cues: Ask me anything. I'll tell you what I know.
subtitle: Ask me anything. I'll tell you what I know.

character: Warden Isolde, keeper of the Waystone Camp
text_with_cues: Five Wardens. Take them one at a time. And come home between them, will you? [softly] I worry.
subtitle: Five Wardens. Take them one at a time. And come home between them, will you? I worry.

character: Warden Isolde, keeper of the Waystone Camp
text_with_cues: [softly] You did it. All of it. Do you feel that? The wind's changed. The waystones are singing a new song.
subtitle: You did it. All of it. Do you feel that? The wind's changed. The waystones are singing a new song.

character: Warden Isolde, keeper of the Waystone Camp
text_with_cues: When you first woke here, the world was holding its breath. Now it's breathing again, and it's because of you.
subtitle: When you first woke here, the world was holding its breath. Now it's breathing again, and it's because of you.

character: Warden Isolde, keeper of the Waystone Camp
text_with_cues: Whatever you do next, build, wander, rest, it'll remember you kindly. [warmly] And so will I.
subtitle: Whatever you do next, build, wander, rest, it'll remember you kindly. And so will I.

character: Warden Isolde, keeper of the Waystone Camp
text_with_cues: [surprised] Is that Bram's stew? You made it? [laughs softly] Thank you. I'll pretend I wasn't hungry.
subtitle: Is that Bram's stew? You made it? Thank you. I'll pretend I wasn't hungry.

character: Warden Isolde, keeper of the Waystone Camp
text_with_cues: The waystones sing different songs now. Happier ones, I think. Safe roads, traveller.
subtitle: The waystones sing different songs now. Happier ones, I think. Safe roads, traveller.

character: Warden Isolde, keeper of the Waystone Camp
text_with_cues: Safe roads, traveller. The waystones remember you.
subtitle: Safe roads, traveller. The waystones remember you.

character: Marta Ironvein, smith to the Wardens
text_with_cues: So Isolde sent me another one. Good. Mind the sparks. Marta Ironvein, smith to the Wardens.
subtitle: So Isolde sent me another one. Good. Mind the sparks. Marta Ironvein, smith to the Wardens.

character: Marta Ironvein, smith to the Wardens
text_with_cues: Out there, things hit hard and they don't take turns. So you'll learn two things before you leave my yard.
subtitle: Out there, things hit hard and they don't take turns. So you'll learn two things before you leave my yard.

character: Marta Ironvein, smith to the Wardens
text_with_cues: First, the roll. Tap the dodge key, Left Alt unless you've changed it, and you'll roll clear. For a breath, nothing can touch you.
subtitle: First, the roll. Tap the dodge key, Left Alt unless you've changed it, and you'll roll clear. For a breath, nothing can touch you.

character: Marta Ironvein, smith to the Wardens
text_with_cues: Second, the parry. Raise a shield, or your blade, the instant before a blow lands, and it'll bounce right back at them.
subtitle: Second, the parry. Raise a shield, or your blade, the instant before a blow lands, and it'll bounce right back at them.

character: Marta Ironvein, smith to the Wardens
text_with_cues: The dummy in the yard swings slow and honest. Roll under one swing, then parry the next. [impatient] Go on.
subtitle: The dummy in the yard swings slow and honest. Roll under one swing, then parry the next. Go on.

character: Marta Ironvein, smith to the Wardens
text_with_cues: Roll. When the dummy swings, tap dodge and get out from under it. Don't think. Roll.
subtitle: Roll. When the dummy swings, tap dodge and get out from under it. Don't think. Roll.

character: Marta Ironvein, smith to the Wardens
text_with_cues: Now the parry. Block the instant before it hits. Too early and you're just holding a shield. [dryly] Too late and you're holding your nose.
subtitle: Now the parry. Block the instant before it hits. Too early and you're just holding a shield. Too late and you're holding your nose.

character: Marta Ironvein, smith to the Wardens
text_with_cues: Mind the sparks. Marta Ironvein, smith to the Wardens.
subtitle: Mind the sparks. Marta Ironvein, smith to the Wardens.

character: Marta Ironvein, smith to the Wardens
text_with_cues: The beasts out here grow strange parts. Bring them to me with a few Marks, and I'll make you something worth swinging.
subtitle: The beasts out here grow strange parts. Bring them to me with a few Marks, and I'll make you something worth swinging.

character: Marta Ironvein, smith to the Wardens
text_with_cues: Back for steel? Good. Steel's always the answer. [beat] Usually.
subtitle: Back for steel? Good. Steel's always the answer. Usually.

character: Marta Ironvein, smith to the Wardens
text_with_cues: Ember cores from the ashen husks make a blade that burns. Crystal from the shardlings sings when you swing it.
subtitle: Ember cores from the ashen husks make a blade that burns. Crystal from the shardlings sings when you swing it.

character: Marta Ironvein, smith to the Wardens
text_with_cues: Lurker fangs make a hook that drags, gear springs a maul that kicks, rime cores a spear that bites cold. Bring me the pieces.
subtitle: Lurker fangs make a hook that drags, gear springs a maul that kicks, rime cores a spear that bites cold. Bring me the pieces.

character: Marta Ironvein, smith to the Wardens
text_with_cues: That blade of yours has some miles on it. Weapons remember, out here. Every fight. Every kill. Some of them start to want more.
subtitle: That blade of yours has some miles on it. Weapons remember, out here. Every fight. Every kill. Some of them start to want more.

character: Marta Ironvein, smith to the Wardens
text_with_cues: Bring me a weapon that's ready to wake, and the parts it asks for, and we'll see what it wants to become. You'll swing the hammer, mind. I don't do all the work.
subtitle: Bring me a weapon that's ready to wake, and the parts it asks for, and we'll see what it wants to become. You'll swing the hammer, mind. I don't do all the work.

character: Marta Ironvein, smith to the Wardens
text_with_cues: When it's ready, it hums. You'll see it in the journal, and on the blade. Then bring it here with what it asks for.
subtitle: When it's ready, it hums. You'll see it in the journal, and on the blade. Then bring it here with what it asks for.

character: Marta Ironvein, smith to the Wardens
text_with_cues: No hum yet. Keep fighting. Weapons are like people. They grow when they're used.
subtitle: No hum yet. Keep fighting. Weapons are like people. They grow when they're used.

character: Marta Ironvein, smith to the Wardens
text_with_cues: It's humming. I can hear it from here. To the anvil, then.
subtitle: It's humming. I can hear it from here. To the anvil, then.

character: Marta Ironvein, smith to the Wardens
text_with_cues: Strike when the metal glows gold. Not before. Not after. [grins] And keep your fingers where I can see them.
subtitle: Strike when the metal glows gold. Not before. Not after. And keep your fingers where I can see them.

character: Marta Ironvein, smith to the Wardens
text_with_cues: There. Feel the weight change? That's not the steel. That's the weapon deciding it likes you.
subtitle: There. Feel the weight change? That's not the steel. That's the weapon deciding it likes you.

character: Marta Ironvein, smith to the Wardens
text_with_cues: Bring me any weapon that hums, any time. The anvil's yours.
subtitle: Bring me any weapon that hums, any time. The anvil's yours.

character: Quartermaster Bram
text_with_cues: Isolde sent you? Then you're welcome at my stall. Name's Bram. I keep this camp fed, lit and stitched together.
subtitle: Isolde sent you? Then you're welcome at my stall. Name's Bram. I keep this camp fed, lit and stitched together.

character: Quartermaster Bram
text_with_cues: Here's twenty-five Marks to start you off. Nobody walks out of my camp with an empty purse. [gruff] That's not charity, mind. It's an investment.
subtitle: Here's twenty-five Marks to start you off. Nobody walks out of my camp with an empty purse. That's not charity, mind. It's an investment.

character: Quartermaster Bram
text_with_cues: Now. Prices out here move like weather. Sell me the same thing ten times and I'll pay you less each time. Bring me something rare from far away and I'll pay you more.
subtitle: Now. Prices out here move like weather. Sell me the same thing ten times and I'll pay you less each time. Bring me something rare from far away and I'll pay you more.

character: Quartermaster Bram
text_with_cues: Go on, sell me something. Anything. Then buy something you need. That's the whole trick of it.
subtitle: Go on, sell me something. Anything. Then buy something you need. That's the whole trick of it.

character: Quartermaster Bram
text_with_cues: Sell me something, then buy something. Open my stall and have a look. Go on.
subtitle: Sell me something, then buy something. Open my stall and have a look. Go on.

character: Quartermaster Bram
text_with_cues: A new face. Name's Bram. Quartermaster. Isolde will want to see you first, mind. She's by the waystone.
subtitle: A new face. Name's Bram. Quartermaster. Isolde will want to see you first, mind. She's by the waystone.

character: Quartermaster Bram
text_with_cues: Back again? Good. Let's see what you need.
subtitle: Back again? Good. Let's see what you need.

character: Quartermaster Bram
text_with_cues: Every merchant pays more for what's scarce where they stand. Ember glass is cheap where it's made, and dear in the snow.
subtitle: Every merchant pays more for what's scarce where they stand. Ember glass is cheap where it's made, and dear in the snow.

character: Quartermaster Bram
text_with_cues: Carry goods between the keepers and you'll make a fortune. Or lose your boots to a lurker. [chuckles] That's trade.
subtitle: Carry goods between the keepers and you'll make a fortune. Or lose your boots to a lurker. That's trade.

character: Quartermaster Bram
text_with_cues: And don't sell all your fangs to one stall in one day. I'll stop wanting them. So will everyone.
subtitle: And don't sell all your fangs to one stall in one day. I'll stop wanting them. So will everyone.

character: Quartermaster Bram
text_with_cues: You know what this camp's missing? A proper meal. Not jerky. Not bread. A stew that remembers its grandmother.
subtitle: You know what this camp's missing? A proper meal. Not jerky. Not bread. A stew that remembers its grandmother.

character: Quartermaster Bram
text_with_cues: Bring me two raw beef, three carrots, two potatoes, and an ember core for the warmth. I'll teach you to cook it yourself.
subtitle: Bring me two raw beef, three carrots, two potatoes, and an ember core for the warmth. I'll teach you to cook it yourself.

character: Quartermaster Bram
text_with_cues: Two beef, three carrots, two potatoes and an ember core. [gruff] Mind you don't eat them on the way.
subtitle: Two beef, three carrots, two potatoes and an ember core. Mind you don't eat them on the way.

character: Quartermaster Bram
text_with_cues: You've got it all? Good. To the pot.
subtitle: You've got it all? Good. To the pot.

character: Quartermaster Bram
text_with_cues: Add each thing when the broth tells you, and keep it stirring. A stew's like a camp. Neglect it and it burns.
subtitle: Add each thing when the broth tells you, and keep it stirring. A stew's like a camp. Neglect it and it burns.

character: Quartermaster Bram
text_with_cues: The pot's still warm. Give it another go.
subtitle: The pot's still warm. Give it another go.

character: Quartermaster Bram
text_with_cues: Now take a bowl to Isolde. She forgets to eat when she's worrying, and she's always worrying.
subtitle: Now take a bowl to Isolde. She forgets to eat when she's worrying, and she's always worrying.

character: Quartermaster Bram
text_with_cues: She ate it? All of it? [laughs] Ha! Here. Take this purse knot. Coins like it. They stay.
subtitle: She ate it? All of it? Ha! Here. Take this purse knot. Coins like it. They stay.

character: Wren Halloway, Cartographers’ Guild
text_with_cues: Oh! A new face. Wren Halloway, Cartographers' Guild. I map the places that won't sit still.
subtitle: Oh! A new face. Wren Halloway, Cartographers' Guild. I map the places that won't sit still.

character: Wren Halloway, Cartographers’ Guild
text_with_cues: If you're looking for something out there, I can probably mark it on your map. Probably. And I keep the Guild Ledger, so your Marks can sleep somewhere safer than your pockets.
subtitle: If you're looking for something out there, I can probably mark it on your map. Probably. And I keep the Guild Ledger, so your Marks can sleep somewhere safer than your pockets.

character: Wren Halloway, Cartographers’ Guild
text_with_cues: Back from the edges? Tell me everything. [excited] Or at least, tell me where.
subtitle: Back from the edges? Tell me everything. Or at least, tell me where.

character: Wren Halloway, Cartographers’ Guild
text_with_cues: Of course. What are you after?
subtitle: Of course. What are you after?

character: Wren Halloway, Cartographers’ Guild
text_with_cues: [lowers voice] The Warden's Ladder. An old gate, dark stone, a stone that glows. Step through and you're somewhere else entirely.
subtitle: The Warden's Ladder. An old gate, dark stone, a stone that glows. Step through and you're somewhere else entirely.

character: Wren Halloway, Cartographers’ Guild
text_with_cues: Fifty floors, they say, each one meaner than the last. The Guild has never mapped past the fifth. [brightly] I've marked the nearest gate for you!
subtitle: Fifty floors, they say, each one meaner than the last. The Guild has never mapped past the fifth. I've marked the nearest gate for you!

character: Wren Halloway, Cartographers’ Guild
text_with_cues: There. It's on your map now. Follow the light, and mind the edges. The edges are where maps get hungry.
subtitle: There. It's on your map now. Follow the light, and mind the edges. The edges are where maps get hungry.

character: Wren Halloway, Cartographers’ Guild
text_with_cues: There's a gazebo where the moon comes down to rest. A tower crowned with a crescent. A mushroom house frozen into the ice. And an airship that never quite lands.
subtitle: There's a gazebo where the moon comes down to rest. A tower crowned with a crescent. A mushroom house frozen into the ice. And an airship that never quite lands.

character: Wren Halloway, Cartographers’ Guild
text_with_cues: Each has a keeper, and a waystone. Touch it, and you can come back whenever you like. It's the closest thing to cheating the Guild allows.
subtitle: Each has a keeper, and a waystone. Touch it, and you can come back whenever you like. It's the closest thing to cheating the Guild allows.

character: Wren Halloway, Cartographers’ Guild
text_with_cues: You've got good boots and a curious face. How'd you like to do some real surveying? The Guild pays, and I pay better.
subtitle: You've got good boots and a curious face. How'd you like to do some real surveying? The Guild pays, and I pay better.

character: Wren Halloway, Cartographers’ Guild
text_with_cues: Take this sextant. Find three landmarks, stand by their waystones and take a sighting. The trick is the wind. Hold your breath, and wait for the needle to settle.
subtitle: Take this sextant. Find three landmarks, stand by their waystones and take a sighting. The trick is the wind. Hold your breath, and wait for the needle to settle.

character: Wren Halloway, Cartographers’ Guild
text_with_cues: Bring me three good sightings and I'll give you something that makes the whole world smaller. [laughs] Well. Easier to fall off.
subtitle: Bring me three good sightings and I'll give you something that makes the whole world smaller. Well. Easier to fall off.

character: Wren Halloway, Cartographers’ Guild
text_with_cues: Three sightings, three landmarks. The sextant counts them for you. Mind the needle.
subtitle: Three sightings, three landmarks. The sextant counts them for you. Mind the needle.

character: Wren Halloway, Cartographers’ Guild
text_with_cues: Three! [delighted] Beautiful. These are the best sightings I've seen since, well, since mine.
subtitle: Three! Beautiful. These are the best sightings I've seen since, well, since mine.

character: Wren Halloway, Cartographers’ Guild
text_with_cues: Here. Moth-silk. Hold your jump while you fall and it'll catch the wind. The moths spun it, so be nice to moths.
subtitle: Here. Moth-silk. Hold your jump while you fall and it'll catch the wind. The moths spun it, so be nice to moths.

character: Wren Halloway, Cartographers’ Guild
text_with_cues: The five glyph tablets? I've a list. Of course I have a list.
subtitle: The five glyph tablets? I've a list. Of course I have a list.

character: Wren Halloway, Cartographers’ Guild
text_with_cues: One in the sunken bog temple. One in the frozen mage tower. One in the buried obelisk, out in the dunes. One in the overgrown ziggurat. And one in a moonlit clearing in the Duskpine. I'll mark whichever is nearest.
subtitle: One in the sunken bog temple. One in the frozen mage tower. One in the buried obelisk, out in the dunes. One in the overgrown ziggurat. And one in a moonlit clearing in the Duskpine. I'll mark whichever is nearest.

character: Rook, keeper of the landings in the Warden's Ladder
text_with_cues: [cheerfully] Ah! A climber! Welcome to Rook's Landing. Warm fire, fair prices, no refunds.
subtitle: Ah! A climber! Welcome to Rook's Landing. Warm fire, fair prices, no refunds.

character: Rook, keeper of the landings in the Warden's Ladder
text_with_cues: I've been on this Ladder longer than your grandmother's grandmother. Never reached the top. Never fell off, either. [chuckles] I take the back stairs.
subtitle: I've been on this Ladder longer than your grandmother's grandmother. Never reached the top. Never fell off, either. I take the back stairs.

character: Rook, keeper of the landings in the Warden's Ladder
text_with_cues: [warmly] Back again! Sit, sit. The fire doesn't charge.
subtitle: Back again! Sit, sit. The fire doesn't charge.

character: Rook, keeper of the landings in the Warden's Ladder
text_with_cues: Five floors to the next landing. Every tenth, a Warden's echo waits. Not the Warden, mind. Just the memory of one. [whispers] Memories hit just as hard.
subtitle: Five floors to the next landing. Every tenth, a Warden's echo waits. Not the Warden, mind. Just the memory of one. Memories hit just as hard.

character: Rook, keeper of the landings in the Warden's Ladder
text_with_cues: Stock up. Drink something red. And if the Ladder throws you out, come back. It always lets you back in.
subtitle: Stock up. Drink something red. And if the Ladder throws you out, come back. It always lets you back in.

character: Rook, keeper of the landings in the Warden's Ladder
text_with_cues: The Edict-writers built this place to prove their Wardens. I swept the floors. [laughs] Then they left, and I stayed.
subtitle: The Edict-writers built this place to prove their Wardens. I swept the floors. Then they left, and I stayed.

character: Rook, keeper of the landings in the Warden's Ladder
text_with_cues: Somebody has to keep the fires lit. And somebody has to sell you potions at a very reasonable markup.
subtitle: Somebody has to keep the fires lit. And somebody has to sell you potions at a very reasonable markup.

character: Stargazer Selene, keeper of the Moon Gazebo
text_with_cues: [whispers] Hush. The moon is listening. I'm Selene. I keep the gazebo, and I count the stars that fall.
subtitle: Hush. The moon is listening. I'm Selene. I keep the gazebo, and I count the stars that fall.

character: Stargazer Selene, keeper of the Moon Gazebo
text_with_cues: Every night there is one fewer. I think someone is collecting them.
subtitle: Every night there is one fewer. I think someone is collecting them.

character: Stargazer Selene, keeper of the Moon Gazebo
text_with_cues: The sky is kind tonight. Or it is pretending to be.
subtitle: The sky is kind tonight. Or it is pretending to be.

character: Stargazer Selene, keeper of the Moon Gazebo
text_with_cues: Light remembers. A fallen star is a memory the sky let go of.
subtitle: Light remembers. A fallen star is a memory the sky let go of.

character: Stargazer Selene, keeper of the Moon Gazebo
text_with_cues: The Bureau keeps some of them in jars, I'm told. I hope they whisper to them. [sadly] Stars get lonely.
subtitle: The Bureau keeps some of them in jars, I'm told. I hope they whisper to them. Stars get lonely.

character: Stargazer Selene, keeper of the Moon Gazebo
text_with_cues: There was a constellation here once. The Lost Moth. Its stars fell one by one, and with them went the gazebo's song.
subtitle: There was a constellation here once. The Lost Moth. Its stars fell one by one, and with them went the gazebo's song.

character: Stargazer Selene, keeper of the Moon Gazebo
text_with_cues: The old star chart was torn into three. One piece lies in the crystal observatory in the Shardfields. One at the aurora shrine in the Glimmerfrost. And one in the crater where a star once fell, out on the Ember Steppe.
subtitle: The old star chart was torn into three. One piece lies in the crystal observatory in the Shardfields. One at the aurora shrine in the Glimmerfrost. And one in the crater where a star once fell, out on the Ember Steppe.

character: Stargazer Selene, keeper of the Moon Gazebo
text_with_cues: Bring the pieces to me, and we will put the Moth back in the sky.
subtitle: Bring the pieces to me, and we will put the Moth back in the sky.

character: Stargazer Selene, keeper of the Moon Gazebo
text_with_cues: Three pieces. The observatory, the aurora shrine, the crater. The sky can wait. It is very patient.
subtitle: Three pieces. The observatory, the aurora shrine, the crater. The sky can wait. It is very patient.

character: Stargazer Selene, keeper of the Moon Gazebo
text_with_cues: [breathless] You found them. All three. Let me... yes. There. The Lost Moth.
subtitle: You found them. All three. Let me... yes. There. The Lost Moth.

character: Stargazer Selene, keeper of the Moon Gazebo
text_with_cues: Now the hard part. The dials on the gazebo's floor turn the old stars. Turn them until the sky above matches the chart. But only at night. The stars are shy.
subtitle: Now the hard part. The dials on the gazebo's floor turn the old stars. Turn them until the sky above matches the chart. But only at night. The stars are shy.

character: Stargazer Selene, keeper of the Moon Gazebo
text_with_cues: Wait for the night. Then turn the dials. [softly] I will keep watch with you.
subtitle: Wait for the night. Then turn the dials. I will keep watch with you.

character: Stargazer Selene, keeper of the Moon Gazebo
text_with_cues: The dials are waiting. Turn each one until its star sits where the chart says. You will feel it settle.
subtitle: The dials are waiting. Turn each one until its star sits where the chart says. You will feel it settle.

character: Stargazer Selene, keeper of the Moon Gazebo
text_with_cues: [softly] Do you hear it? The gazebo is singing again. The Moth is home.
subtitle: Do you hear it? The gazebo is singing again. The Moth is home.

character: Stargazer Selene, keeper of the Moon Gazebo
text_with_cues: These were made from the last of the fallen starlight. Featherstep boots. Jump, and then jump again, as if the air were a stair.
subtitle: These were made from the last of the fallen starlight. Featherstep boots. Jump, and then jump again, as if the air were a stair.

character: Captain Odo Brassmere, master of the Wayfarer
text_with_cues: [booming] Ahoy, groundling! Captain Odo Brassmere, of the Wayfarer. Best ship in the sky. [beat] Only ship in the sky, come to think of it.
subtitle: Ahoy, groundling! Captain Odo Brassmere, of the Wayfarer. Best ship in the sky. Only ship in the sky, come to think of it.

character: Captain Odo Brassmere, master of the Wayfarer
text_with_cues: She's moored for repairs. Bring me gear springs and clockwork, and I'll make it worth your while.
subtitle: She's moored for repairs. Bring me gear springs and clockwork, and I'll make it worth your while.

character: Captain Odo Brassmere, master of the Wayfarer
text_with_cues: Wind's from the west today. Good sailing weather, if one had a sail.
subtitle: Wind's from the west today. Good sailing weather, if one had a sail.

character: Captain Odo Brassmere, master of the Wayfarer
text_with_cues: There are whales up there, you know. Great gentle things. They sing at dawn.
subtitle: There are whales up there, you know. Great gentle things. They sing at dawn.

character: Captain Odo Brassmere, master of the Wayfarer
text_with_cues: Lovely creatures. Just don't let one sit on your balloon. [laughs] Ask me how I know.
subtitle: Lovely creatures. Just don't let one sit on your balloon. Ask me how I know.

character: Captain Odo Brassmere, master of the Wayfarer
text_with_cues: Here's the trouble. The Wayfarer's rudder springs are shot, and her clock-heart is skipping. I need six gear springs and two clockwork fragments.
subtitle: Here's the trouble. The Wayfarer's rudder springs are shot, and her clock-heart is skipping. I need six gear springs and two clockwork fragments.

character: Captain Odo Brassmere, master of the Wayfarer
text_with_cues: Gearhounds carry springs in their bellies, poor things. Clockwork you'll find wherever the King's toys wander.
subtitle: Gearhounds carry springs in their bellies, poor things. Clockwork you'll find wherever the King's toys wander.

character: Captain Odo Brassmere, master of the Wayfarer
text_with_cues: Six springs and two fragments, groundling. The sky won't wait forever. [beat] Actually, it will. But I won't.
subtitle: Six springs and two fragments, groundling. The sky won't wait forever. Actually, it will. But I won't.

character: Captain Odo Brassmere, master of the Wayfarer
text_with_cues: [laughs] Look at that! Springs, clockwork, and not a single finger missing. Splendid.
subtitle: Look at that! Springs, clockwork, and not a single finger missing. Splendid.

character: Captain Odo Brassmere, master of the Wayfarer
text_with_cues: Now, before I trust her with passengers, someone has to test the wings. Climb the tower, take this practice wing, and fly through every ring before the sand runs out.
subtitle: Now, before I trust her with passengers, someone has to test the wings. Climb the tower, take this practice wing, and fly through every ring before the sand runs out.

character: Captain Odo Brassmere, master of the Wayfarer
text_with_cues: The rings, groundling! Top of the mooring tower, jump, and steer for the lights. Sixty seconds, all eight rings.
subtitle: The rings, groundling! Top of the mooring tower, jump, and steer for the lights. Sixty seconds, all eight rings.

character: Captain Odo Brassmere, master of the Wayfarer
text_with_cues: [delighted] Ha! You fly like you were hatched up there! Here. My old hook. Point it at anything and it'll pull you there, or pull it to you. [beat] Don't point it at me.
subtitle: Ha! You fly like you were hatched up there! Here. My old hook. Point it at anything and it'll pull you there, or pull it to you. Don't point it at me.

character: Captain Odo Brassmere, master of the Wayfarer
text_with_cues: And any time you want to go somewhere far, come and see me. For a few Marks, the Wayfarer will take you.
subtitle: And any time you want to go somewhere far, come and see me. For a few Marks, the Wayfarer will take you.

character: Captain Odo Brassmere, master of the Wayfarer
text_with_cues: Where to, groundling? Thirty Marks a leg, and I throw in the view for free.
subtitle: Where to, groundling? Thirty Marks a leg, and I throw in the view for free.

character: Fen-Keeper Mab, witch of the black water
text_with_cues: [cackles] Heh. Another one wading in. I'm Mab. The fen is mine, and I'm the fen's.
subtitle: Heh. Another one wading in. I'm Mab. The fen is mine, and I'm the fen's.

character: Fen-Keeper Mab, witch of the black water
text_with_cues: Mind the lurkers. They look like logs, right up until they don't.
subtitle: Mind the lurkers. They look like logs, right up until they don't.

character: Fen-Keeper Mab, witch of the black water
text_with_cues: Still breathing? The fen likes you, then. [sly] Or it's saving you for later.
subtitle: Still breathing? The fen likes you, then. Or it's saving you for later.

character: Fen-Keeper Mab, witch of the black water
text_with_cues: Brew before you fight, not after. And never answer the bog when it calls your name.
subtitle: Brew before you fight, not after. And never answer the bog when it calls your name.

character: Fen-Keeper Mab, witch of the black water
text_with_cues: Want to cross my fen without wet boots? Heh. There's a charm for that. But a charm needs a brew, and a brew needs a fool to fetch for it.
subtitle: Want to cross my fen without wet boots? Heh. There's a charm for that. But a charm needs a brew, and a brew needs a fool to fetch for it.

character: Fen-Keeper Mab, witch of the black water
text_with_cues: Three lurker fangs, one lump of bog amber, and two pinches of moth dust. Bring them, and mind the logs.
subtitle: Three lurker fangs, one lump of bog amber, and two pinches of moth dust. Bring them, and mind the logs.

character: Fen-Keeper Mab, witch of the black water
text_with_cues: Fangs, amber, dust. I'll not repeat myself a third time. [cackles] I will, actually. Fangs. Amber. Dust.
subtitle: Fangs, amber, dust. I'll not repeat myself a third time. I will, actually. Fangs. Amber. Dust.

character: Fen-Keeper Mab, witch of the black water
text_with_cues: Good, good. Now, the cauldron. Drop each one in when the brew turns the right colour, and stir with the bubbles, not against them.
subtitle: Good, good. Now, the cauldron. Drop each one in when the brew turns the right colour, and stir with the bubbles, not against them.

character: Fen-Keeper Mab, witch of the black water
text_with_cues: The cauldron's still hot. Again, and gently this time.
subtitle: The cauldron's still hot. Again, and gently this time.

character: Fen-Keeper Mab, witch of the black water
text_with_cues: Drink it, and walk out to the dead tree in the middle of the water and back. If you come back dry, the charm is yours.
subtitle: Drink it, and walk out to the dead tree in the middle of the water and back. If you come back dry, the charm is yours.

character: Fen-Keeper Mab, witch of the black water
text_with_cues: If you come back wet, well. [cackles] It's a learning experience.
subtitle: If you come back wet, well. It's a learning experience.

character: Fen-Keeper Mab, witch of the black water
text_with_cues: [cackles] Dry as a bone! Take the charm. It'll hold you up on water, and on lava that's had a good long think about cooling.
subtitle: Dry as a bone! Take the charm. It'll hold you up on water, and on lava that's had a good long think about cooling.

character: Fen-Keeper Mab, witch of the black water
text_with_cues: Don't make a habit of the lava.
subtitle: Don't make a habit of the lava.

character: Torvald the Hunter
text_with_cues: Stranger. Sit by the fire if you like. Torvald. I hunt what hunts the valley.
subtitle: Stranger. Sit by the fire if you like. Torvald. I hunt what hunts the valley.

character: Torvald the Hunter
text_with_cues: The rimehorns are restless this year. And something walks the frozen peaks. Taller than the trees.
subtitle: The rimehorns are restless this year. And something walks the frozen peaks. Taller than the trees.

character: Torvald the Hunter
text_with_cues: The fire's warm. The meat's fresh. Sit.
subtitle: The fire's warm. The meat's fresh. Sit.

character: Torvald the Hunter
text_with_cues: Ice and white fur, and horns like a cathedral's ribs. The old songs call it the Rimeback.
subtitle: Ice and white fur, and horns like a cathedral's ribs. The old songs call it the Rimeback.

character: Torvald the Hunter
text_with_cues: If you ever see the snow stand up, run. [beat] Then run some more.
subtitle: If you ever see the snow stand up, run. Then run some more.

character: Torvald the Hunter
text_with_cues: The rimehorn alpha has been taking the young ones from the valley. I am old, and my knees are older. You are neither.
subtitle: The rimehorn alpha has been taking the young ones from the valley. I am old, and my knees are older. You are neither.

character: Torvald the Hunter
text_with_cues: Follow its tracks from the lodge. They're deep and wide, and the snow fills them fast. Lose them, and you lose it.
subtitle: Follow its tracks from the lodge. They're deep and wide, and the snow fills them fast. Lose them, and you lose it.

character: Torvald the Hunter
text_with_cues: Its tracks start at the lodge. Watch the snow. The fresh ones still have their edges.
subtitle: Its tracks start at the lodge. Watch the snow. The fresh ones still have their edges.

character: Torvald the Hunter
text_with_cues: You brought down the alpha? [laughs] Then you've earned a contest.
subtitle: You brought down the alpha? Then you've earned a contest.

character: Torvald the Hunter
text_with_cues: Every hunter at this lodge has shot the targets. Hit six of eight, and I'll call you hunter too.
subtitle: Every hunter at this lodge has shot the targets. Hit six of eight, and I'll call you hunter too.

character: Torvald the Hunter
text_with_cues: The targets are set. Six of eight. Breathe out before you loose.
subtitle: The targets are set. Six of eight. Breathe out before you loose.

character: Torvald the Hunter
text_with_cues: Six of eight. Good. Better than I did, my first winter.
subtitle: Six of eight. Good. Better than I did, my first winter.

character: Torvald the Hunter
text_with_cues: Take these claws. They'll let you climb where the rimehorns climb. And the stag, he's taken a liking to you. Whistle, and he'll come.
subtitle: Take these claws. They'll let you climb where the rimehorns climb. And the stag, he's taken a liking to you. Whistle, and he'll come.

character: Torvald the Hunter
text_with_cues: One more thing. The big tracks, the ones as wide as a cart. Those aren't rimehorn. If you ever follow them, go well armed.
subtitle: One more thing. The big tracks, the ones as wide as a cart. Those aren't rimehorn. If you ever follow them, go well armed.

character: Sister Ines, of the Morrow Court
text_with_cues: Peace, traveller. I am Sister Ines, of the Morrow Court. We remember the dead, so that they may rest.
subtitle: Peace, traveller. I am Sister Ines, of the Morrow Court. We remember the dead, so that they may rest.

character: Sister Ines, of the Morrow Court
text_with_cues: The bell of this chapel drowned long ago. Still, some nights, I hear it ring.
subtitle: The bell of this chapel drowned long ago. Still, some nights, I hear it ring.

character: Sister Ines, of the Morrow Court
text_with_cues: Welcome back. The candles burned steady while you were gone.
subtitle: Welcome back. The candles burned steady while you were gone.

character: Sister Ines, of the Morrow Court
text_with_cues: There. Rest a moment. The road will wait for you. It always does.
subtitle: There. Rest a moment. The road will wait for you. It always does.

character: Sister Ines, of the Morrow Court
text_with_cues: Some nights a voice hums near the altar. A child's voice, I think. The bell-ringer's apprentice, who drowned with the bell.
subtitle: Some nights a voice hums near the altar. A child's voice, I think. The bell-ringer's apprentice, who drowned with the bell.

character: Sister Ines, of the Morrow Court
text_with_cues: The bell's rope was carried off by the tide. It lies in the drowned shrine on the coast, if the old records are right. Bring it back, and perhaps she can finish her song.
subtitle: The bell's rope was carried off by the tide. It lies in the drowned shrine on the coast, if the old records are right. Bring it back, and perhaps she can finish her song.

character: Sister Ines, of the Morrow Court
text_with_cues: The drowned shrine, on the coast. Go carefully. The sea keeps what it takes.
subtitle: The drowned shrine, on the coast. Go carefully. The sea keeps what it takes.

character: Sister Ines, of the Morrow Court
text_with_cues: The rope! It's still whole. Bring it to the altar bells, and listen.
subtitle: The rope! It's still whole. Bring it to the altar bells, and listen.

character: Sister Ines, of the Morrow Court
text_with_cues: When the humming starts, ring the small bells in the same order. [softly] Gently.
subtitle: When the humming starts, ring the small bells in the same order. Gently.

character: Sister Ines, of the Morrow Court
text_with_cues: Ring them as she hums. If you lose the tune, she will hum it again.
subtitle: Ring them as she hums. If you lose the tune, she will hum it again.

character: Sister Ines, of the Morrow Court
text_with_cues: [softly] She finished it. Did you hear? The whole song.
subtitle: She finished it. Did you hear? The whole song.

character: Sister Ines, of the Morrow Court
text_with_cues: This bell is hers. Ring it, and it will lift you, the way a song lifts a heavy heart. Up, and up.
subtitle: This bell is hers. Ring it, and it will lift you, the way a song lifts a heavy heart. Up, and up.

character: Sister Ines, of the Morrow Court
text_with_cues: The records speak of a lich who hid his heart in three places. A barrow on the Vesper Downs. An ossuary gate in the Pale Reach. And his own necropolis.
subtitle: The records speak of a lich who hid his heart in three places. A barrow on the Vesper Downs. An ossuary gate in the Pale Reach. And his own necropolis.

character: Sister Ines, of the Morrow Court
text_with_cues: Break all three, or he will not stay down. [quietly] The Court will pray for you. It helps more than you'd think.
subtitle: Break all three, or he will not stay down. The Court will pray for you. It helps more than you'd think.

character: Rashid of the Sands, master of the caravan
text_with_cues: Welcome to the Hourglass, friend. Rashid, master of this caravan. The water is free. [playful] Everything else, we can discuss.
subtitle: Welcome to the Hourglass, friend. Rashid, master of this caravan. The water is free. Everything else, we can discuss.

character: Rashid of the Sands, master of the caravan
text_with_cues: Ah, my friend returns. The sand remembers you, and so do I.
subtitle: Ah, my friend returns. The sand remembers you, and so do I.

character: Rashid of the Sands, master of the caravan
text_with_cues: It tells the hours with its shadow. But at noon, sometimes, it tells the wrong one.
subtitle: It tells the hours with its shadow. But at noon, sometimes, it tells the wrong one.

character: Rashid of the Sands, master of the caravan
text_with_cues: On those days the sand remembers things it shouldn't. We pack up early.
subtitle: On those days the sand remembers things it shouldn't. We pack up early.

character: Rashid of the Sands, master of the caravan
text_with_cues: Three days ago my sister's caravan left for the nomad camps of the Ember Steppe. Twelve camels, eight drivers, a cargo of spice. It never arrived.
subtitle: Three days ago my sister's caravan left for the nomad camps of the Ember Steppe. Twelve camels, eight drivers, a cargo of spice. It never arrived.

character: Rashid of the Sands, master of the caravan
text_with_cues: No sandstorm. No bandits seen. Just silence. Find out what happened to them, and you will have a friend in every market I trade in.
subtitle: No sandstorm. No bandits seen. Just silence. Find out what happened to them, and you will have a friend in every market I trade in.

character: Rashid of the Sands, master of the caravan
text_with_cues: Start where they were last seen, the old road east of here. Look for anything out of place. Sand hides things, but it is a poor liar.
subtitle: Start where they were last seen, the old road east of here. Look for anything out of place. Sand hides things, but it is a poor liar.

character: Rashid of the Sands, master of the caravan
text_with_cues: You found the wagon, the manifest, and the tracks. So. Where did they go? You saw what I did not.
subtitle: You found the wagon, the manifest, and the tracks. So. Where did they go? You saw what I did not.

character: Rashid of the Sands, master of the caravan
text_with_cues: [doubtful] Hm. That does not fit the tracks, my friend. Look at what you found again. Sand is a poor liar, remember.
subtitle: Hm. That does not fit the tracks, my friend. Look at what you found again. Sand is a poor liar, remember.

character: Rashid of the Sands, master of the caravan
text_with_cues: The obelisk! Of course. They hid from the storm-eaters. Go, quickly. If they hid there, something chased them in.
subtitle: The obelisk! Of course. They hid from the storm-eaters. Go, quickly. If they hid there, something chased them in.

character: Rashid of the Sands, master of the caravan
text_with_cues: The buried obelisk, east and south. Bring them home, friend.
subtitle: The buried obelisk, east and south. Bring them home, friend.

character: Rashid of the Sands, master of the caravan
text_with_cues: My sister. Alive. And most of the spice, which she says I care about more. [laughs] She is wrong. Mostly.
subtitle: My sister. Alive. And most of the spice, which she says I care about more. She is wrong. Mostly.

character: Rashid of the Sands, master of the caravan
text_with_cues: Take this seal. Show it to any Guild merchant, and they will treat you as family. Which means slightly less robbery.
subtitle: Take this seal. Show it to any Guild merchant, and they will treat you as family. Which means slightly less robbery.

character: Leyla of the Sands, Rashid's sister
elevenlabs_voice: (search the library: "Middle Eastern female warm mature")
text_with_cues: [whispering] Shh. Keep your voice down. The storm-eaters hunt by sound.
subtitle: Shh. Keep your voice down. The storm-eaters hunt by sound.

character: Leyla of the Sands, Rashid's sister
elevenlabs_voice: (search the library: "Middle Eastern female warm mature")
text_with_cues: If you're going back to the Hourglass, find a merchant called Rashid. Tell him his sister is alive, and very, very annoyed.
subtitle: If you're going back to the Hourglass, find a merchant called Rashid. Tell him his sister is alive, and very, very annoyed.

character: Leyla of the Sands, Rashid's sister
elevenlabs_voice: (search the library: "Middle Eastern female warm mature")
text_with_cues: You're not a storm-eater. [relieved] Rashid sent you? Of course he did. He'd send the whole Guild if it didn't cost him a coin.
subtitle: You're not a storm-eater. Rashid sent you? Of course he did. He'd send the whole Guild if it didn't cost him a coin.

character: Leyla of the Sands, Rashid's sister
elevenlabs_voice: (search the library: "Middle Eastern female warm mature")
text_with_cues: We hid down here when the sand opened and those things came out. Eight drivers, all alive. Mostly whole.
subtitle: We hid down here when the sand opened and those things came out. Eight drivers, all alive. Mostly whole.

character: Leyla of the Sands, Rashid's sister
elevenlabs_voice: (search the library: "Middle Eastern female warm mature")
text_with_cues: Then we walk at dusk. Tell my brother we're coming. [smiles] And that I counted the spice.
subtitle: Then we walk at dusk. Tell my brother we're coming. And that I counted the spice.

character: Leyla of the Sands, Rashid's sister
elevenlabs_voice: (search the library: "Middle Eastern female warm mature")
text_with_cues: We leave at dusk. Go on ahead, and tell Rashid to put the kettle on.
subtitle: We leave at dusk. Go on ahead, and tell Rashid to put the kettle on.

character: Leyla of the Sands, Rashid's sister
elevenlabs_voice: (search the library: "Middle Eastern female warm mature")
text_with_cues: The road's quiet again. The sand owes you one, traveller. So do I.
subtitle: The road's quiet again. The sand owes you one, traveller. So do I.

character: Akane, last disciple of the Lantern Dojo
text_with_cues: You walk into the Lantern Dojo with your boots on. Bold. I am Akane, the last disciple of this house.
subtitle: You walk into the Lantern Dojo with your boots on. Bold. I am Akane, the last disciple of this house.

character: Akane, last disciple of the Lantern Dojo
text_with_cues: My master became the Ashen Shogun. Every lantern on these walls is a life he took. If you have come to challenge him, you must first face me.
subtitle: My master became the Ashen Shogun. Every lantern on these walls is a life he took. If you have come to challenge him, you must first face me.

character: Akane, last disciple of the Lantern Dojo
text_with_cues: The lanterns flicker when you enter. They remember you.
subtitle: The lanterns flicker when you enter. They remember you.

character: Akane, last disciple of the Lantern Dojo
text_with_cues: [quietly] Not yet. You still smell of the camp's woodsmoke. He has burned a hundred who were braver than you look.
subtitle: Not yet. You still smell of the camp's woodsmoke. He has burned a hundred who were braver than you look.

character: Akane, last disciple of the Lantern Dojo
text_with_cues: When the Warden of the waystones speaks to you of the five Wardens, come back. The lanterns will still be burning. They always are.
subtitle: When the Warden of the waystones speaks to you of the five Wardens, come back. The lanterns will still be burning. They always are.

character: Akane, last disciple of the Lantern Dojo
text_with_cues: He was the gentlest man I knew. He swore to guard the blossom country forever, and the world took him at his word.
subtitle: He was the gentlest man I knew. He swore to guard the blossom country forever, and the world took him at his word.

character: Akane, last disciple of the Lantern Dojo
text_with_cues: Forever is too long for a promise. It burned him to ash, and left the oath walking.
subtitle: Forever is too long for a promise. It burned him to ash, and left the oath walking.

character: Akane, last disciple of the Lantern Dojo
text_with_cues: The Duel of Lanterns has one rule. Only a perfect parry may strike. Any other blow, and the lanterns go dark.
subtitle: The Duel of Lanterns has one rule. Only a perfect parry may strike. Any other blow, and the lanterns go dark.

character: Akane, last disciple of the Lantern Dojo
text_with_cues: Turn my blade aside five times, and I will give you his challenge lantern. [quietly] And perhaps, peace.
subtitle: Turn my blade aside five times, and I will give you his challenge lantern. And perhaps, peace.

character: Akane, last disciple of the Lantern Dojo
text_with_cues: [breathing hard] Five. You turned my blade five times. Take the lantern.
subtitle: Five. You turned my blade five times. Take the lantern.

character: Akane, last disciple of the Lantern Dojo
text_with_cues: Light it at the dojo's heart, and he will come. Do not let him reach the hundredth lantern.
subtitle: Light it at the dojo's heart, and he will come. Do not let him reach the hundredth lantern.

character: The Ashen Shogun
text_with_cues: You came for the lanterns. Every one is a life I took.
subtitle: You came for the lanterns. Every one is a life I took.

character: The Ashen Shogun
text_with_cues: [slowly] Add yours.
subtitle: Add yours.

character: The Ashen Shogun
text_with_cues: Which of us is the ash? Choose.
subtitle: Which of us is the ash? Choose.

character: The Ashen Shogun
text_with_cues: A hundred lanterns. [quietly] Light the last one.
subtitle: A hundred lanterns. Light the last one.

character: The Ashen Shogun
text_with_cues: The wind is clean again.
subtitle: The wind is clean again.

character: The Ashen Shogun
text_with_cues: Take my lantern. Walk where I could not.
subtitle: Take my lantern. Walk where I could not.

character: The Crimson Lich
text_with_cues: Ah. A visitor who still has a heartbeat. [amused] How quaint.
subtitle: Ah. A visitor who still has a heartbeat. How quaint.

character: The Crimson Lich
text_with_cues: Kneel, and I shall make it quick. Stand, and I shall make it last.
subtitle: Kneel, and I shall make it quick. Stand, and I shall make it last.

character: The Crimson Lich
text_with_cues: My obelisks drink. You will tire long before they do.
subtitle: My obelisks drink. You will tire long before they do.

character: The Crimson Lich
text_with_cues: [roaring] Rise. All of you. RISE.
subtitle: Rise. All of you. RISE.

character: The Crimson Lich
text_with_cues: [laughs] Did you think death was something I had not already survived?
subtitle: Did you think death was something I had not already survived?

character: The Crimson Lich
text_with_cues: The phylacteries. You found them. [weakly] Clever.
subtitle: The phylacteries. You found them. Clever.

character: The Crimson Lich
text_with_cues: Then let me, at last, be still.
subtitle: Then let me, at last, be still.

character: The King of Seconds
elevenlabs_voice: Victor – The Cunning Villain – Posh British
text_with_cues: Late. Everyone is always late. Shall we see how late you are?
subtitle: Late. Everyone is always late. Shall we see how late you are?

character: The King of Seconds
elevenlabs_voice: Victor – The Cunning Villain – Posh British
text_with_cues: A trade, then. A second of my power for every second you spare me. Tick, tock. Decide.
subtitle: A trade, then. A second of my power for every second you spare me. Tick, tock. Decide.

character: The King of Seconds
elevenlabs_voice: Victor – The Cunning Villain – Posh British
text_with_cues: [slowing] Tick. Tock. Tick.
subtitle: Tick. Tock. Tick.

character: The Bell-Ringer
text_with_cues: [whispers] Ring. Must ring. Must...
subtitle: Ring. Must ring. Must...

character: The Bell-Ringer
text_with_cues: [whispers] That was... my name. Yes. That was me.
subtitle: That was... my name. Yes. That was me.

character: The Bell-Ringer
text_with_cues: [whispers] Quiet. So quiet now.
subtitle: Quiet. So quiet now.

character: The Gilded Warden
text_with_cues: None pass the Gilded Vault without the five glyphs. You carry them.
subtitle: None pass the Gilded Vault without the five glyphs. You carry them.

character: The Gilded Warden
text_with_cues: [resonant] Then be judged.
subtitle: Then be judged.

character: The Gilded Warden
text_with_cues: The shell remembers every blow. So do I.
subtitle: The shell remembers every blow. So do I.

character: The Gilded Warden
text_with_cues: Judgment is not cruelty. It is accounting.
subtitle: Judgment is not cruelty. It is accounting.

character: The Gilded Warden
text_with_cues: The account is settled. Go, traveller. You are owed nothing, and owe nothing.
subtitle: The account is settled. Go, traveller. You are owed nothing, and owe nothing.

character: The Dune Sentinel
text_with_cues: [booming] WHO... WAKES... THE SUN?
subtitle: WHO... WAKES... THE SUN?

character: The Dune Sentinel
text_with_cues: [grinding] Sleep... again...
subtitle: Sleep... again...

character: The Afterworld (chapter openings)
text_with_cues: The world listens. It always has. Today, it heard you wake.
subtitle: The world listens. It always has. Today, it heard you wake.

character: The Afterworld (chapter openings)
text_with_cues: Chapter One. The Listening World. Where the ground hums, a rule has slipped its leash.
subtitle: Chapter One. The Listening World. Where the ground hums, a rule has slipped its leash.

character: The Afterworld (chapter openings)
text_with_cues: Chapter Two. The Three Who Wait. A bell, a clock, and a pilgrim. Each one stuck. Each one waiting for you.
subtitle: Chapter Two. The Three Who Wait. A bell, a clock, and a pilgrim. Each one stuck. Each one waiting for you.

character: The Afterworld (chapter openings)
text_with_cues: Chapter Three. Wardens of the Five Lands. The old guardians never stopped guarding. Not even when they should have.
subtitle: Chapter Three. Wardens of the Five Lands. The old guardians never stopped guarding. Not even when they should have.

character: The Afterworld (chapter openings)
text_with_cues: And the world, at last, let out its breath.
subtitle: And the world, at last, let out its breath.
